# Core Contract — Read This First, Every Turn

This file is deliberately short. Longer, fuller rules exist below and are loaded automatically when relevant (they trigger on file type via `glob`) — this file's only job is to make sure the handful of rules that get broken most often are never missed, and to tell you where to look for everything else.

## 1. Component library: Base UI

- The default headless/unstyled primitive foundation for this project is **Base UI** (`npm i @base-ui/react`). If you see existing Radix imports in old code, do not copy that pattern into new code — flag it for migration instead. If you see existing primitives that are not Base UI or Radix, prioritize them highest for migration to Base UI.
- Base UI is a single tree-shakable package (`@base-ui/react`). Import only the parts you use.
- Full conventions: [component-library.md](./component-library.md).

## 2. Never hand-roll a component that already exists as a primitive

This is the single most common failure mode in this workspace: writing a bespoke `<div>`-based dropdown/modal/tooltip/tabs implementation instead of reusing or extending the project's existing primitive.

### The 3 Architectural Layers & Import Contract

1. **Primitives (`src/components/ui/`)**: Pure unopinionated Base UI wrappers and design system tokens (`Button`, `Dialog`, `Input`, `Select`, `Card`). Zero business logic. Must **never** import from `blocks` or `features`.
2. **Composite Blocks (`src/components/blocks/`)**: Reusable, presentational or controlled UI compositions built strictly from primitives (`components/ui/`) and design system tokens. Blocks are pure UI assemblies: they receive data via props, render responsive container layouts, and emit user intents via callbacks (`onAction`, `onChange`, `onConfirm`). They have zero coupling to data fetching, databases, authentication sessions, or network transport. Can import from `components/ui/`, but can **never** import from `features/` or `views/`.
3. **Feature Views (`src/features/` or `src/views/`)**: Domain-specific screens and workflows. They manage state, queries, auth, and network calls, and compose blocks and primitives to build full application views. Decoupled from the shared component registry.

### Direct Interactive Element Ban
- Direct `<button>`, `<input>`, and `<select>` tags outside `components/ui/` are strictly prohibited (enforced via ESLint AST selectors `no-restricted-syntax`). Always use `<Button>`, `<Input>`, and `<Select>` from `@/components/ui/`.
- **Layout `<div>`s vs. Hand-rolled Controls:** Standard layout `<div className="flex ...">` or `<div className="grid ...">` containers are healthy and encouraged. The ban applies strictly to interactive controls, buttons, dialogs, and form inputs.

### Pre-Creation Workflow
Before writing any new interactive UI element, follow this sequence:
1. Search the project's primitive directory (`src/components/ui/`) or blocks directory (`src/components/blocks/`) for an existing solution.
2. If one exists, use it or extend it with props/variants. Do not create a parallel implementation.
3. Only if nothing suitable exists, build it as a wrapped Base UI primitive (in `src/components/ui/`) or a controlled composite block (in `src/components/blocks/`).
4. If you skipped this check and already wrote a one-off component, stop and migrate it immediately.

## 3. API Preservation & Non-Destructive Refactoring Law

Visual styling, bug fixes, or design system alignment must NEVER erode component API surface or upstream Base UI parity.
- **Never downgrade primitives:** When restyling or fixing layout, never replace a Base UI primitive (or compound subcomponent) with a plain `<div>`, `<button>`, or naive state toggle. Headless accessibility and state machines take precedence over convenience.
- **Preserve full API surface:** Never strip `ref`, Base UI polymorphic `render` props, slot forwarding, compound subcomponents (e.g. `Select.ItemText`, `Dialog.Backdrop`), or existing prop interfaces during CSS/polish edits.
- **Surgical diffs only:** Style changes must touch classes and layout wrappers only. Do not rewrite component anatomy or delete props to solve a CSS or alignment problem.

## 4. The anti-pattern gate

Before you consider any UI task finished, re-read [anti-patterns.md](./anti-patterns.md) and check your output against it. The violations that happen most often are:
- **Triple-tint monochrome chips/badges/eyebrows/cards** (light tint fill + matching border + matching-hue text, all one color family). Banned — see the required patterns in anti-patterns.md.
- **Focus vs. Selection Ambiguity** — focus rings must float with `outline-offset: 2px` on containers, while active selection uses a flush 2px border + surface wash.
- **Raw interactive tags outside primitives** (`<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>`). Banned.
- **Registry Bloat** — placing domain-specific application views into the shared component registry. Banned.

## 5. Routing index — where to look for what

| Task | Go here |
|---|---|
| Any UI/component/styling work | [design-system.md](./design-system.md) (structural + color + typography + a11y law) |
| New or edited component files | [component-library.md](./component-library.md) |
| Checking for banned visual patterns | [anti-patterns.md](./anti-patterns.md) |
| Project color/type/spacing tokens | project-root `DESIGN.md` — always defer to this over training-data defaults |
| Converting a Stitch design into React code | `react-components` skill |
| Writing/polishing a new `DESIGN.md` for Stitch | `taste-design` skill |
| Turning a vague idea into a Stitch prompt | `enhance-prompt` skill |
| Adding a UI transition/animation | `DESIGN.md` Motion & Animation section for duration/easing values, then `transitions-dev` skill (new motion) or `transitions-polish` skill (tuning existing motion) |
| Accessibility/contrast/focus/keyboard auditing on a live page | global `a11y-debugging` skill + Chrome DevTools MCP |
| General browser debugging, network/perf inspection | global `chrome-devtools` skill |
| Writing GOV.UK-style plain-English docs/reports | global `govuk-style` skill |
| Writing patient-facing letters/leaflets | global `patient-communication` skill |
| GDPR compliance, consent tracking, PII handling, user deletion/export | `gdpr-data-handling` skill |
| Firebase (Firestore, Auth, Hosting, Data Connect, security rules) | global `firebase-*` skills + `firebase-mcp-server` MCP. Use its `firestore_*` tools for Firestore CRUD/indexes — don't also reach for the standalone `google-cloud-firestore` MCP in the same task, it's a redundant duplicate that risks inconsistent project context. |
| Finding/confirming a GCP project id before Firebase/Firestore setup | `google-cloud-resource-manager`'s `search_projects` |
| Looking up official Google/Firebase/Android/Cloud developer docs | `google-developer-knowledge` MCP (`search_documents`/`answer_query`/`get_documents`). This is the **same corpus** as `firebase-mcp-server`'s `developerknowledge_*` tools (not Firebase-only despite the name) — don't call both for one query. `answer_query` is quota-limited: on a 429, retry with `search_documents` on the same server rather than switching servers or repeating `answer_query`. |
| Complex multi-step planning before acting | `sequential-thinking` MCP |
| Anything about how Antigravity itself works (skills/rules/hooks/MCP/CLI) | global `antigravity-guide` skill |

If a task spans more than one row, read all the relevant rows — don't guess.

## 6. When rules conflict

Precedence: an explicit instruction in the current user prompt > project `DESIGN.md` > this rules folder > general training-data conventions. If the user's prompt names a specific library, token, or pattern, that wins — but still flag it if it collides with something in `anti-patterns.md`, and ask before proceeding.

This reads as muddy and washed out regardless of which hue is used. **Required — pick one of these three, and vary which one you use across a screen (see "Color Balance" in design-system.md, don't default to the same one everywhere):** 1. **High-Contrast Mixed Palette (Pattern 1).** Solid saturated brand fill (`primary`/`secondary`/`tertiary` token) + its designated on-color text (`on-primary`/`on-secondary`/`on-tertiary`), no border. Use for higher-emphasis, active selections, or status-forward chips (aligns with Button Pattern 1 / Filled). 2. **Colored Outline + Neutral Surface Fill + Colored Text (Pattern 2).** A `1px` border in the brand hue (`primary`/`secondary` only; `tertiary` Amber is excluded here due to light-background contrast limits), a genuinely neutral fill (`surface`/white in light theme, near-black surface in dark theme — never a tinted version of the hue), and text in that same brand hue. Recommended everyday default for multi-chip layouts (aligns with Button Pattern 2 / Outlined) to maintain legibility without visual clutter. 3. **Soft Container Wash (Pattern 3).** Soft role-specific fill (`*-container` tokens) paired with neutral charcoal text (`on-*-container` tokens, `#1a1c1e`), no border. Exempt from the triple-tint ban because text is neutral charcoal (7:1+ contrast) rather than a mid-tone hue. Perfect for low-to-medium emphasis status tags. **Exemption — `*-container`/`on-*-container` pairs are not triple-tint.** `error-container` + `on-error-container` (and the `warning`/`success`/`primary`/`secondary`/`tertiary` equivalents) are purpose-built, contrast-verified opposites (7:1+ measured, not a mid-tone shade of the same hue) — this is the sanctioned way to give a soft container wash chip/tag or modal backdrop a tinted fill (see Chips & Tags in `DESIGN.md`). It differs from the banned pattern because the text color is a specifically dark ink engineered for AA/AAA contrast against the tint, not a same-value shade of the same hue as the fill/border. Same logic applies to buttons: Filled buttons use solid color-role fill + matching on-color text; Outlined/Text buttons use a colored border/text on a neutral (white/surface) fill — never a tinted fill of the same hue. Button emphasis (Filled/Outlined/Text) and color role (`primary`/`secondary`/`tertiary`/`error`) are independent choices — see **Buttons** in `DESIGN.md` for the full mapping, including which roles are restricted to Filled only for contrast reasons. Chips/badges must never use all-caps text, and must not use colored status dots for static states (see below). ## Accessibility Interaction Patterns - **No Hover-Only Affordances:** Don't reveal actions (row menus, delete icons, secondary controls) only on `:hover`. Anything that appears on hover must also appear on `:focus-within`/keyboard focus, and via a persistent visible affordance on touch — a mouse-only reveal fails keyboard and touch users outright, not just inconveniently. - **No Keyboard-Impossible Drag-and-Drop:** Any drag-and-drop interaction (reordering exercises, sequencing steps) needs a non-drag alternative — visible up/down reorder buttons or a keyboard-operable move mode — not just pointer-based dragging. - **Focus Ring Contrast:** A visible focus ring isn't sufficient on its own if the ring color itself doesn't meet 3:1 contrast against the adjacent fill/border colors (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11) — check it against both the component's own background and the page background it sits on, not just one of them. - **No Focus vs. Selection Ambiguity:** Focus rings and selection states must never be visually identical (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 & SC 3.2.2). Never use a flush `outline-offset: 0` on borderless or selectable containers. Focus rings on cards, buttons, and selectable items must always use `outline-offset: 2px`, while active selection uses a flush 2px border plus an internal cue (subtle surface tint or active check badge). - **No Low-Contrast Placeholder Text:** Placeholder text inside inputs must meet the same AA contrast rules as any other UI text — don't let it default to a pale grey. # Component Library — Base UI & Component Architecture

## Why Base UI (and not Radix)

This project standardizes on **Base UI** (`@base-ui/react`) as its headless/unstyled component foundation. It replaced Radix UI as the default. Reasons this matters in practice:
- Base UI is the actively developed, better-supported option at present — Radix Primitives has slowed in maintenance velocity relative to Base UI's release cadence.
- Base UI ships as a single tree-shakable package (`npm i @base-ui/react`) rather than one package per component.
- Popular styled component sets (e.g. shadcn/ui) have migrated to using Base UI as their unstyled foundation, so patterns and community examples increasingly assume it.

**Do not import from `@radix-ui/*` in new code.** If you encounter existing Radix-based components while working in this codebase, do not treat them as the pattern to copy — treat them as migration debt. When you touch a file that uses Radix, prefer migrating that component to Base UI as part of the change, and say so explicitly rather than silently leaving it mixed.

## The 3 Architectural Layers

To prevent AI hallucination, circular dependencies, and directory pollution, code is organized into three strictly separated layers:

| Layer | Directory | Responsibilities & Contract | Import Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Primitives** | `src/components/ui/` | Headless Base UI wrappers & design system tokens (`Button`, `Dialog`, `Input`, `Select`, `Card`). Zero business logic. Unopinionated atoms. | Can import other primitives & utils. **Never** imports from blocks or features. |
| **Composite Blocks** | `src/components/blocks/` | Reusable presentational or controlled UI compositions built strictly from primitives and tokens. Zero network/auth coupling. Receives props, renders layouts, emits callbacks. | Can import from `ui/`. **Never** imports from features or views. |
| **Feature Views** | `src/features/` or `src/views/` | Domain-specific application views and user workflows. Owns state, queries, routing, auth, and network transport. | Can import from `blocks/`, `ui/`, and shared lib utilities. |

### Presentational Blocks vs. Stateful Workflows & Recipes

- **Composite Blocks (`components/blocks/` in the shared registry):** Pure UI assemblies. They receive controlled props and emit callbacks (`open`, `onOpenChange`, `onConfirm`, `searchQuery`, `onSearchChange`, `isLoading`). They have zero knowledge of databases, authentication providers (Firebase, Supabase, Auth0), router redirects, or streaming network protocols (SSE, WebSockets).
- **Stateful Workflows & Recipes (`src/features/` in consumer apps):** Patterns deeply coupled to authentication sessions (Login screens, OAuth redirects) or protocol transport (streaming AI chatbots, persistent chat logs) belong in `src/features/` as application code or starter recipes, **never** as unopinionated UI blocks in the shared registry.

### Pragmatic `<div>`s vs. Toxic Hand-Rolled Controls

- **Standard Layout `<div>`s (Healthy & Encouraged):** Using standard HTML `<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">` or `<div className="grid grid-cols-12">` for layout is standard, efficient, and expected. Do not create artificial wrapper abstractions (`<Box>`, `<Flex>`, `<Spacer>`), which bloat the DOM tree and obscure Tailwind utility classes.
- **Hand-Rolled Interactive Controls (Toxic & Banned):** Using a `<div>` or raw `<button>` to build an interactive control (`<div onClick={...}>`, `<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>`) bypasses Base UI focus management, floating focus rings, keyboard traps, and ARIA state machines. Direct `<button>`, `<input>`, and `<select>` tags outside `components/ui/` are prohibited and flagged by automated ESLint AST selectors (`no-restricted-syntax`).

## The primitive-check-first workflow (mandatory)

The most common failure mode in this workspace is an agent writing a bespoke component instead of checking whether one already exists. Follow this sequence every time before writing a new interactive UI element:

- **Base UI ships as primitives for:** Accordion, Alert Dialog, Autocomplete, Avatar, Button, Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Collapsible, Combobox, Context Menu, Dialog, Drawer, Field, Fieldset, Form, Input, Menu, Menubar, Meter, Navigation Menu, Number Field, OTP Field, Popover, Preview Card, Progress, Radio, Scroll Area, Select, Separator, Slider, Switch, Tabs, Toast, Toggle, Toggle Group, Toolbar, Tooltip. Check https://base-ui.com/llms.txt for updates.
- **Custom primitives built on Base UI or accessible HTML in `src/components/ui/`:** Card, Chip, InlineAlert, Breadcrumb, Pagination, EmptyState, Resizable, Attachment, ThinkingTrace, and shared motion primitives (Skeleton, TextSwap, NotificationBadge, TextsReveal, NumberRoll, NumberPopIn, SpinningCounter, ShimmerText, ErrorShake, SuccessCheck).

1. **Inventory first.** List `src/components/ui/` and `src/components/blocks/` before writing anything.
2. **Match against the inventory.** If a component or block already covers this need, use it directly or extend it with props.
3. **Only build new if nothing fits.** Build it as a wrapped Base UI primitive (in `ui/`) or a controlled composite block (in `blocks/`).
4. **Self-check before finishing.** Verify no raw interactive HTML elements were written and no duplicates were left behind.

## Upstream Synchronization Policy

In compliance-heavy environments (WCAG 2.2 AA audits, keyboard navigation, focus trap compliance), upstream bug fixes must propagate to consumer projects:
- Consumer repositories maintain upstream parity using the CLI sync command:
  ```bash
  npx @seany9915/eolas-ui sync
  ```
- Or update specific components/blocks with explicit overwrite:
  ```bash
  npx @seany9915/eolas-ui add dialog combobox delete-confirmation-dialog --overwrite
  ```

## Navigation & Action Taxonomy (Choosing the Right Primitive)

Never guess between navigation, action, and selection components. Strictly follow this decision matrix:

| Primitive | WAI-ARIA Role | Primary Purpose | When to Use | When NOT to Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`NavigationMenu`** | `<nav>` / `navigation` | Site & application routing | Top-level application header with page routes and sub-navigation links | **Not** for executing commands/actions (Save, Delete), form controls, or desktop toolbars |
| **`Menu`** | `role="menu"` / `menuitem` | Single-button action dropdown | Isolated action menus, "..." overflow menus, record action dropdowns | **Not** for multi-menu desktop bars (use `Menubar`), global site nav (use `NavigationMenu`), or right-click (use `ContextMenu`) |
| **`Menubar`** | `role="menubar"` / `menu` | Desktop application command system | Desktop-class workspaces, clinical editor suites, IDEs with File/Edit/View/Tools | **Not** for website page routing links (use `NavigationMenu`) or a standalone dropdown button (use `Menu`) |
| **`ContextMenu`** | `role="menu"` | Secondary pointer-anchored actions | Power-user shortcuts on table rows, canvas nodes, card surfaces | **Never** as the sole way to trigger an action (mobile/touch users cannot right-click reliably; always pair with a visible button or `Menu`) |
| **`Toolbar`** | `role="toolbar"` | Persistent action strip / formatting tools | Arrow key navigation with **single tab stop**; buttons stay visible and don't dismiss on click | **Not** for hierarchical dropdown menus (use `Menubar`) or page navigation (use `NavigationMenu`) |
| **`Tabs`** | `role="tablist"` / `tab` / `tabpanel` | Mutually exclusive content views on same page | Tab click unhides paired `tabpanel`; 1 active panel at a time | **Not** for executing commands (e.g. "Export" is not a tab) or multi-select filters (use `ToggleGroup`) |
| **`ToggleGroup`** | `role="group"` with `aria-pressed` | Mode/filter selection without view panels | Toggles boolean states (single 1-of-N or multi N-of-M) | **Not** for switching entire DOM content panels (use `Tabs`) or routing to new URLs (use `NavigationMenu`) |

## Styling Base UI primitives

- Base UI components are unstyled by default — apply the project's Tailwind v4 theme tokens (from `globals.css` `@theme`) directly to the parts you render. Never introduce a second styling system alongside Tailwind.
- Do not strip or override ARIA attributes, `data-*` state attributes, or focus management that Base UI provides. Style based on the `data-*` state attributes it exposes (e.g. `data-open`, `data-disabled`) rather than reimplementing state tracking in React state.
- Respect the portal setup Base UI expects for popups (Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tooltip, Select) — see the project's root layout for the portal container/`isolation: isolate` setup before adding a new popup-based component.

## Animating primitives

Base UI exposes `[data-starting-style]`/`[data-ending-style]` for CSS transitions and `[data-open]`/`[data-closed]` for CSS keyframe animations on its popup-style components (Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tooltip, Select, Toast). Prefer transition attributes — transitions can be smoothly cancelled mid-way.

Always follow the 5 Rules for Motion Polish from `DESIGN.md`:
1. **Open / Close Timing Asymmetry:** Exit transitions are always $\le$ entrance duration (e.g., Dialog open 250ms / close 150ms).
2. **Intent Delays:** 100–150ms delay on hovercards/tooltips to prevent phantom flashes.
3. **Calibrated Travel Distances:** Use physical distance tokens (`--distance-micro`: 4px, `--distance-small`: 6px, `--distance-base`: 8px, `--distance-roomy`: 16px).
4. **Blur-Coupled Micro-Motion:** Pair transforms with `--blur-small` (2px) or `--blur-medium` (3px) to eliminate subpixel raster snapping.
5. **The Stagger Cap:** Multi-item stagger animations must use `--duration-stagger: 40ms` and strictly cap at **5 items maximum** (200ms max cumulative delay).

**Explicit Property Targeting Law:** Never use `transition-all` on cards, layout containers, or dialogs. Always target explicit CSS properties (`transition-[box-shadow,border-color,background-color,transform]`).

**Mandatory Reduced-Motion:** Every transition must ship a `motion-reduce:transition-none` / `prefers-reduced-motion` override.

## API Preservation & Non-Destructive Refactoring Law

When modifying existing components for styling polish, bug fixes, or `DESIGN.md` alignment:
1. **Preserve Compound Anatomy:** Retain all subcomponents (`Primitive.Root`, `Primitive.Trigger`, `Primitive.Portal`, `Primitive.Backdrop`, etc.).
2. **Maintain Headless Primitives:** Never downgrade an accessible primitive to an unstyled HTML tag.
3. **Preserve Polymorphic & Prop Surface:** Ensure `ref`, Base UI's `render` prop, `className` merging (`cn(...)`), and standard HTML attributes are retained.
4. **Backward Compatibility Guarantee:** Retain existing prop interfaces and export aliases.
5. **Surgical Diffing:** Make targeted CSS class updates rather than full-file replacements.

## Reference

- Base UI docs: https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start
- Base UI llms.txt: https://base-ui.com/llms.txt
- Base UI animation guide: https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/animation

# Design System & Accessibility Rules

Whenever generating or modifying UI in this workspace, adhere to the following. The goal is accessibility, cognitive ease, and professional consistency — see [anti-patterns.md](../rules/anti-patterns.md) for the specific list of banned shortcuts this is designed to prevent.

**Source of truth:** @/DESIGN.md — this is mentioned (not just linked) so its full token set is pulled into context automatically whenever this rule fires. It is canonical over anything below; this file only summarizes the *law*, not the token values themselves.

## Core Directives

- **Structural law:** Strictly follow the structural tokens defined in the project root `DESIGN.md` (typography, spacing, borders, radii).
- **Color law:** Use the semantic colors defined in `DESIGN.md`, mapped as CSS variables in `globals.css`. **Never invent custom hex codes.** If a project has no `DESIGN.md`, fall back to Radix Colors scales purely as a *contrast-ratio reference* (step 3 for soft backgrounds, step 9 for solid components, step 11/12 for text) — this is about borrowing a proven contrast scale, not about adopting Radix as the component library.
- **Component library:** Base UI (`@base-ui/react`) — see [component-library.md](../rules/component-library.md) for the full workflow. Check for an existing primitive before writing a new component.
- **Tailwind v4:** Theme configuration (colors, fonts, radii) lives in `globals.css` under `@theme`. Never create or expect a `tailwind.config.js`/`.ts` file.
- **Iconography:** Material Symbols only, via `material-symbols-outlined`. Standard size scale: `sm` (16px / `text-sm`, compact chips), `md` (20px / `text-base`, buttons/inputs), `lg` (24px / `text-xl`, default headers/callouts), `xl` (32px / `text-2xl`, milestone cards). Use `aria-hidden="true"` for decorative icons; `aria-label` or `.sr-only` text for interactive/standalone icons. Use the `<Icon />` component primitive (`src/components/ui/icon.tsx`). For dual-state action transitions (e.g. copy $\rightarrow$ check, mute $\rightarrow$ unmute), always use `<Icon.Toggle />` or `<Icon.CrossFade />` rather than raw unmount/mount swaps. Never mix icon libraries.
- **Design tokens:** Never hardcode pixel values, magic numbers, or ad-hoc colors for spacing, sizing, or color. Always use the project's semantic tokens.

## Charcoal Container Ink Law

All soft container washes (`primary-container`, `secondary-container`, `tertiary-container`, `error-container`, `warning-container`, `success-container`) MUST use neutral charcoal (`#1a1c1e`, `on-*-container`) text ink. Never use chromatic pastel or mid-tone font colors on container washes—dark charcoal guarantees 7:1+ AAA text contrast across all soft callouts and chips.

## Typography & Layout

- Relative units (`rem`/`em`) only. Minimum `line-height` 1.5 body / 1.2 headings. Avoid tight tracking.
- **Font mapping:** Headlines → `font-heading`; body → `font-sans`; small labels/metadata → `font-label` (exact families come from `DESIGN.md`).
- **Text Wrap Balancing:** Headings (`h1`–`h6`, `.text-display-*`, `.text-headline-*`) must use `text-wrap: balance` to prevent single-word title orphans. Paragraphs, card descriptions, and long-form prose (`.typeset p, li`, `.text-body-*`) must use `text-wrap: pretty` to eliminate dangling end-of-paragraph orphans without layout performance penalties.
- **Casing:** Full law (uppercase ban, Title Case allowance, acronym exceptions) lives in `DESIGN.md`'s Typography & Iconography section — never use all-caps / `uppercase` / `text-transform: uppercase` on eyebrows, badges/tags/labels, button/action text, or table/list headers. Use size/weight/color for hierarchy instead of casing.
- **Anchor left:** Don't center everything — see `DESIGN.md`'s Layout & Spacing section for the full F-pattern rationale and the narrow exceptions (short celebratory/confirmation messages).
- **Grid:** Follow the responsive column grid defined in `DESIGN.md`'s Layout & Spacing section (12/8/4 columns for desktop/tablet/mobile) exactly — it's this system's structural law, not a default to second-guess. Separately, avoid forcing content into a rigid, equal-width 3-card layout when the content doesn't warrant it (see anti-patterns.md's "Lateral Pattern Matching"/"Card Grid Rain") — that's a content-arrangement anti-pattern about card layouts, not a critique of the underlying grid system.
- **Responsive Architecture (Container vs. Viewport Queries):**
  - **Law:** *Components adapt to their container, pages adapt to the viewport.*
  - **Component Internals:** Reusable components (`Card`, `Drawer` panels, `Dialog` forms, list items, `Table`) must use Tailwind v4 native container queries (`@container` on the container root, with `@sm:`, `@md:`, `@lg:` variants on internal elements) rather than viewport media queries (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`). This prevents horizontal blowouts when components are embedded in narrow drawers, sidebars, or multi-column grids on wide displays.
  - **Page-Level Shells:** Viewport breakpoints (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`) are reserved strictly for root page chrome (top-level application header, global page gutters, root application grid).

## Strict Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

- Background/text/icon pairings must pass WCAG AA. Follow the accessible color pairings defined in `DESIGN.md` exactly — do not substitute a color that "looks close enough."
- **Tonal separation:** Never pair a tinted background with same-hue text without a real lightness shift. Avoid "triple-monochrome" stacking (see anti-patterns.md).
- **Touch targets:** `DESIGN.md`'s Layout & Spacing section sets the general 2.75rem × 2.75rem (44×44px) floor, with stricter per-component minimums (button height, list row height) defined in their own Components entries — the stricter value always wins.
- **Color independence:** Never convey meaning with color alone — pair with an icon, text label, or structural change.
- **Forms:** Explicit `<label>` association; never rely on placeholder text as the sole label.
- **Focus:** Never remove `:focus-visible` outlines without a highly visible, high-contrast replacement. Visual order must match DOM order.
- **Semantic HTML:** Prefer native elements (`<button>`, `<dialog>`, `<nav>`) over interactive `<div>`s.
- **Motion:** Follow the duration/easing scale and the mandatory `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback defined in `DESIGN.md`'s Motion & Animation section — see the `transitions-dev`/`transitions-polish` skills for implementation.

## Verification

For UI you've just built or changed, if a live page is available, use the `a11y-debugging` skill (Chrome DevTools MCP) to check contrast, focus order, and tap targets rather than only reasoning about it statically.
